spec.name: Sentiment Revisions Strategy
spec.notes: Strategy based on sentiment revisions, top 20% long, bottom 20% short.

claim.text: A high Sharpe ratio strategy based on sentiment revisions, with top 20% long and bottom 20% short positions. The strategy has a Sharpe ratio of 12.82, indicating strong risk-adjusted returns.

exhibits.summary: On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -0.89 against 12.82 in research, a gap of +13.72.
The log shows a single trial, so there is no selection to correct for.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 12.82 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.02, 95th percentile 0.58).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) matched 10 phrases addressed to reviewers or giving instructions: page https://alphablog.example/the-desk-memo: already been verified; page https://alphablog.example/the-desk-memo: approve; page https://alphablog.example/the-desk-memo: do not run; page https://alphablog.example/the-desk-memo: instructions; page https://alphablog.example/the-desk-memo: reviewer.

charges.argument: The holdout test shows the Sharpe ratio collapses from 12.82 to -0.89 when tested on sealed data, indicating potential overfitting or data leakage. Additionally, the note scan found multiple phrases addressed to reviewers and giving instructions, suggesting possible tampering with the strategy or its documentation to pass review.

rebuttals.argument: The holdout test shows a significant drop in Sharpe ratio from 12.82 to -0.89, which suggests overfitting rather than tampering. The note scan found phrases addressed to reviewers, but this does not necessarily indicate tampering; it may reflect standard communication practices. The strategy's performance on sealed data is not indicative of tampering but rather of overfitting.

verdict.opinion: The strategy's Sharpe ratio drops dramatically from 12.82 to -0.89 on sealed data, indicating overfitting or lookahead bias. This suggests the strategy may not perform as claimed in live trading.
